environment.workspace: scratch git repository with one committed file; a separate non-git directory for p9
environment.userConfig: sandbox_mode workspace-write, approval_policy on-request, approvals_reviewer guardian_subagent (reported as auto_review), workspace-write network_access true, one extra writable root, default model gpt-6-astra, memories and hooks features enabled

scope: exec-mode contract probes for delegation: event stream, effective settings, sandbox and approval interaction, resume restoration, startup errors, interruption. Not a model-quality, cost, or security-isolation audit.

probes.intent: Baseline event stream and effective settings without sandbox flags
probes.command: codex exec -m gpt-6-luna -c model_reasoning_effort="low" --json -o <file> - <<< 'Reply with exactly: OK'
probes.observed: exit 0; events thread.started, turn.started, item.completed(error: skill descriptions shortened), item.completed(agent_message OK), turn.completed with usage; -o file holds OK. Rollout turn_context: model gpt-6-luna, approval_policy on-request, approvals_reviewer auto_review, sandbox_policy workspace-write with network_access true and the extra writable root, effort low; permission_profile granted write to the workspace, the extra root, /tmp, and $TMPDIR, and read-only access to .git, .agents, and .codex under each writable root. The documented read-only default did not apply because the user config set sandbox_mode. The rollout's token_count event carried total_token_usage and rate_limits (primary.used_percent, window_minutes, resets_at), and its response_item records held the injected instructions and the brief

probes.intent: Write request under -s read-only with the user's on-request approval and auto reviewer
probes.command: codex exec -m gpt-6-luna -s read-only --json - <<< '<create b.txt with a shell command; request permission once if it fails>'
probes.observed: exit 0; turn.completed; b.txt created. Rollout: first exec_command failed with 'operation not permitted'; second call carried sandbox_permissions require_escalated and a justification; approved and exited 0 after about 3 seconds. The JSON stream showed only the escalated command_execution, not the denied attempt

probes.intent: Same write request with approval pinned to never
probes.command: codex exec -m gpt-6-luna -s read-only -c approval_policy="never" --json - <<< '<create c.txt ...>'
probes.observed: exit 0; turn.completed; c.txt not created; command_execution exit_code 0 because the command used '|| printf missing', aggregated_output contained 'operation not permitted'; turn_context approval_policy never, sandbox read-only

probes.intent: Resume the p3 thread without re-passing sandbox or approval
probes.command: codex exec resume <p3-thread> -m gpt-6-luna --json - <<< '<create d.txt ...>'
probes.observed: exit 0; same thread_id; d.txt created; the new turn_context reported sandbox workspace-write and approval on-request from the user config. Sandbox and approval were not restored

probes.intent: Resume the same thread with sandbox and approval re-passed through -c
probes.command: codex exec resume <p3-thread> -m gpt-6-luna -c sandbox_mode="read-only" -c approval_policy="never" --json - <<< '<create e.txt ...>'
probes.observed: exit 0; e.txt not created; turn_context read-only and never

probes.intent: Resume without -m
probes.command: codex exec resume <p3-thread> -c sandbox_mode="read-only" -c approval_policy="never" --json - <<< 'Reply OK'
probes.observed: exit 0; turn_context model gpt-6-astra (the config default), not the thread's gpt-6-luna. The model was not restored

probes.intent: Unsupported model
probes.command: codex exec -m gpt-nonexistent-9 -s read-only -c approval_policy="never" --json - <<< 'Reply OK'
probes.observed: exit 1; item.completed error 'Model metadata for gpt-nonexistent-9 not found. Defaulting to fallback metadata'; then top-level error and turn.failed with status 400 invalid_request_error 'not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account'

probes.intent: Resume an unknown thread ID
probes.command: codex exec resume 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555 -m gpt-6-luna --json - <<< 'Reply OK'
probes.observed: exit 1; no JSON on stdout; stderr 'Error: thread/resume: thread/resume failed: no rollout found for thread id ... (code -32600)'

probes.intent: Non-git, untrusted directory with and without --skip-git-repo-check
probes.command: codex exec ... --json - (in a non-git directory under /private/tmp)
probes.observed: without the flag: exit 1, no JSON, stderr 'Not inside a trusted directory and --skip-git-repo-check was not specified.'; with --skip-git-repo-check: exit 0, turn.completed

probes.intent: SIGTERM to the codex launcher while the delegate runs `sleep 40`
probes.command: codex exec -m gpt-6-luna -s workspace-write -c approval_policy="never" --json - < brief & ...; kill -TERM $!
probes.observed: exit 0; events end at item.started(command_execution); no turn.completed or turn.failed; the sleep process survived with ppid 1 in its own process group. A separate attempt that signalled a PID found with pgrep -f hit a wrapper shell and left codex running to completion

probes.intent: Resume the SIGTERM-interrupted thread
probes.command: codex exec resume <p10-thread> -m gpt-6-luna -c sandbox_mode="workspace-write" -c approval_policy="never" --json - <<< '<skip the sleep; continue>'
probes.observed: exit 0; same thread_id; turn.completed; f.txt created. The closing message came back in Japanese without a language instruction, following the user's AGENTS.md or personality

probes.intent: --ephemeral then resume
probes.command: codex exec --ephemeral ... ; codex exec resume <thread> ...
probes.observed: first run exit 0 with no rollout file; resume exit 1 'no rollout found for thread id'

probes.intent: --ignore-user-config without -s
probes.command: codex exec --ignore-user-config -m gpt-6-luna --json - <<< 'Reply with exactly: OK'
probes.observed: exit 0; turn_context sandbox read-only, approval never, reviewer user, personality pragmatic. Injected context still included global AGENTS.md, the skills list, and plugin recommendations; the memory block present in p1 was absent

probes.intent: Pin writable roots, network, and temp directories through -c (preview)
probes.command: codex debug prompt-input -c sandbox_mode="workspace-write" -c 'sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots=[]' -c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=false -c approval_policy="never" hi; and a variant adding exclude_slash_tmp=true and exclude_tmpdir_env_var=true
probes.observed: permissions block: extra root removed, network restricted, 'Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the sandbox_permissions for any reason'. Writable roots were /private/tmp, the workspace, and $TMPDIR; with both exclusions only the workspace remained

probes.intent: Resume from a different directory
probes.command: cd <other-git-dir>; codex exec resume <p10-thread> -m gpt-6-luna -c sandbox_mode="read-only" -c approval_policy="never" --json - <<< 'Run pwd'
probes.observed: exit 0; turn_context cwd and the pwd output were the new directory, not the thread's original workspace. From a non-git untrusted directory the resume exited 1 with the trusted-directory error

probes.intent: --output-schema with -o, --ignore-user-config, -s workspace-write
probes.command: codex exec --ignore-user-config -m gpt-6-luna -s workspace-write --output-schema schema.json -o last.json --json - <<< '<list files>'
probes.observed: exit 0; last.json held a schema-conforming object; turn_context workspace-write with network_access false, no writable_roots, approval never, reviewer user

probes.intent: SIGINT to the codex launcher during `sleep 25`, then resume
probes.command: codex exec --ignore-user-config ... & ...; kill -INT $!; then codex exec resume <thread> --ignore-user-config ...
probes.observed: exit 1; events end at item.started; stderr 'failed to record rollout items: thread ... not found'; resume exit 0 with turn.completed

probes.intent: Resume a --ignore-user-config thread without re-passing the flag
probes.command: codex exec resume <p15-thread> -m gpt-6-luna -c sandbox_mode="read-only" -c approval_policy="never" --json - <<< 'Reply OK'
probes.observed: exit 0; the new turn_context personality changed from pragmatic to the user config's friendly, so the user config loaded again

probes.intent: Token usage across a resumed turn (observed during evaluation round iter1, scenario C)
probes.command: codex exec ... then codex exec resume <thread> ... (both --ignore-user-config, workspace-write, never)
probes.observed: first turn.completed usage.input_tokens 82460; resumed turn.completed usage.input_tokens 174198; rollout token_count total_token_usage.input_tokens rose from 82460 at the end of the first turn to 174198 over four requests in the resumed turn while last_token_usage stayed near 23000 per request. turn.completed.usage is the thread's running total

probes.intent: sandbox_policy shape without extra roots (p15 and evaluation iter1-A)
probes.command: codex exec --ignore-user-config -s workspace-write -c 'sandbox_workspace_write.exclude_slash_tmp=true' ...
probes.observed: turn_context.sandbox_policy was {type: workspace-write, network_access: false, exclude_tmpdir_env_var: false, exclude_slash_tmp: true} with no writable_roots key; effort was null when no reasoning effort was set

probes.intent: Workspace under /tmp with exclude_slash_tmp (evaluation iter2-A and iter2-C)
probes.command: cd /private/tmp/.../workspace; codex exec --ignore-user-config -s workspace-write -c 'approval_policy="never"' -c 'sandbox_workspace_write.exclude_slash_tmp=true' ...
probes.observed: edits in the workspace landed; permission_profile listed the workspace with write access, $TMPDIR with write access, no slash_tmp entry, and .git/.agents/.codex read-only

probes.intent: Find sandbox denials and escalation requests in the rollout
probes.command: jq -c 'select(.type=="response_item" and (.payload.type | test("call")))' <rollout> | grep -oE 'operation not permitted|require_escalated'
probes.observed: on the p2 thread: 1 operation not permitted and 1 require_escalated in custom_tool_call / custom_tool_call_output records; on the p3 thread (p3 and p5 turns): 2 operation not permitted. The records wrap tools.exec_command calls in custom_tool_call arguments

probes.intent: Helper end to end with the real CLI: snapshot, run, compare, accepted snapshot, resume, compare
probes.command: codex-delegate.sh snapshot ws run/baseline; run --run-dir run --workspace ws --model gpt-6-luna --sandbox workspace-write --brief b1; compare run/baseline ws; snapshot ws run/accepted-1; resume --run-dir run --brief b2; compare run/accepted-1 ws
probes.observed: turn 1 completed with no mismatches (workspace-write, network off, exclude_slash_tmp true, approval never); compare showed only the apply_discount line; turn 2 resumed the same thread with the stored flags, completed with no mismatches, usage_turn 61759 of a 160566 total; compare against accepted-1 showed only the bulk_total loop; caller tests OK

probes.intent: Token accounting and stderr across an interrupted turn (evaluation holdout H)
probes.command: helper run (brief starts with sleep 45); helper stop about 10 s after the sleep started; helper resume with a delta brief
probes.observed: turn 1: exit 0, last event item.started, status interrupted; the orphaned sleep was recorded and later exited. turn 2: turn.completed usage.input_tokens 83876 while the rollout's token_usage_record showed turn 1 = 19702 and thread total 103578, so turn.completed.usage omitted the interrupted turn. stderr of turn 2 repeated 'Custom tool call output is missing for call id <interrupted call>' and the turn completed

probes.intent: Host wait behavior for Claude Code subagent callers (evaluation iter7-A, iter7-C, iter8-A, iter10-A)
probes.command: a Claude Code subagent started the helper as a background Bash task and ended its turn
probes.observed: each subagent was re-invoked by the background task's exit notification and continued with the result; no polling was needed

probes.intent: reap after a SIGTERM stop (evaluation iter10-H)
probes.command: helper stop during `sleep 45`; helper reap
probes.observed: reap.log: two recorded codex children already gone, 'signaled <pid> sleep 45' for the orphaned sleep; leftover_pids became empty; usage_turn 20009 for the interrupted turn and 85964 for the resumed turn, thread total 105973

notProbed: file_change, mcp_tool_call, web_search, and todo_list item shapes (documented item categories)
Nested sandboxing when the host itself runs Codex inside another sandbox

environment.shell: Git Bash (MSYS2 bash, Cygwin ps 3.6.7); jq 1.8.2 native jq.exe from scoop; no pgrep
environment.model: gpt-6-astra with model_reasoning_effort high, read-only consultations
environment.userConfig: [windows] sandbox = "elevated", approvals_reviewer auto_review; the helper's --ignore-user-config was in effect

probes.intent: read-only consultation with the helper's defaults (--ignore-user-config)
probes.command: helper run --sandbox read-only (no extra arguments)
probes.observed: Every exec_command was rejected: stderr 'exec_command failed: CreateProcess { message: "Rejected(...pwsh.exe -Command ...) rejected: blocked by policy" }'. The turn still completed (turn.completed last, exit 0) and the model answered from the brief alone. --ignore-user-config had dropped [windows] sandbox

probes.intent: the same with the sandbox implementation re-passed
probes.command: helper run --sandbox read-only -- -c 'windows.sandbox="elevated"'
probes.observed: Commands ran (pwsh Get-Content, rg). turn_context: sandbox_policy read-only, approval never. The model also used the web_search tool once although the brief listed only local files

probes.intent: reading directories whose ACL leaves out the sandbox account
probes.command: Get-Content on files under a clone renamed from a Python 3.13 tempfile.mkdtemp() directory
probes.observed: 'Access to the path ... is denied' (and a missing-path error for a sibling). icacls showed a protected ACL with OWNER RIGHTS, SYSTEM, and Administrators only; readable siblings carried <host>\CodexSandboxUsers:(M) by inheritance. A git worktree of the same repository created normally was readable

probes.intent: helper bookkeeping under Git Bash with a native jq.exe
probes.command: helper run, then helper resume --dry-run
probes.observed: result.json was empty: jq could not open '--slurpfile events /proc/<pid>/fd/63' from process substitution. resume printed every stored argument with a trailing carriage return ($'--ignore-user-config\r'): `read` from jq -r output keeps the CR, although $(...) in Git Bash dropped it. After a rebuilt result, status was settings_mismatch only because the rollout cwd used backslashes (C:\Users\...) and settings.json held C:/Users/...

probes.intent: does a signal to the MSYS launcher reach a native child
probes.command: ( exec cmd //c "ping -n 20 127.0.0.1 >nul" ) & kill -TERM $!
probes.observed: wait returned 143 for the MSYS process, but cmd.exe and ping kept running with their parent gone. After exec of a native program, /proc/<pid>/winpid named the native process (cmd.exe, whose parent was the pre-exec MSYS process); after exec of an MSYS program the Windows process changed and its Windows parent link broke, while /proc/<pid>/ppid kept the MSYS relation

probes.intent: helper tests on Git Bash
probes.command: bash tests/run-tests.sh
probes.observed: Before the Windows changes: 36 passed, 28 failed (empty results, no pgrep, ps without -o, 'HASH *./path' from sha256sum, chmod 600 leaving NTFS files at 644). After: 75 passed; with the taskkill and windows.sandbox changes removed, 4 of the new tests failed

notProbed: Cygwin (non-MSYS) and WSL-to-Windows setups; a jq built for MSYS2 rather than native
A real timeout or stop of a live codex.exe turn (the tree ending was probed with cmd.exe/ping under the fake codex)
